title: Datadog Pricing 2026: Cost Per Product and Host
summary: Datadog pricing uses separate metering for each product. See what Infrastructure Pro and other plans cost to determine your monthly spending.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Datadog costs and limits teams hit


The remaining surprises are billed on units you don't control directly: custom metric series, indexed log events, and hosts counted by Datadog's rules. Each has a cap you can set before the invoice arrives.


### Datadog custom metrics and cardinality costs


Count unique series, not metrics, because Datadog meters custom metrics by unique series, meaning each metric name combined with each distinct set of tag values. Every host includes an allotment, and anything past it is billed in blocks.


Add a single tag such as user ID or container ID and one metric can multiply into thousands of series, so the charge follows your tagging habits, not your metric count.


The cap is to review tags before they ship and to remove high-cardinality tags you never query.

### Datadog log ingestion versus indexing costs


Ingestion is the cheap step: Datadog accepts the log and bills per gigabyte. Indexing is where logs become searchable, and it's billed per event, on top of ingestion. A team that sends everything and indexes everything pays twice for logs nobody searches.


Set exclusion filters on indexes, and keep low-value logs in archives instead of live search.


### How Datadog counts hosts and overages


Hosts are counted by what Datadog sees reporting, not by what you provision. Short-lived instances, autoscaling bursts, and containers on nodes can each push the count above what you budgeted.


Many plans bill on a high-water-mark style measure rather than an average, so one spike can set the month's number.


### Cap Datadog costs with usage alerts


You can alert on estimated usage the way you alert on CPU, because Datadog exposes its own usage data. Create monitors on custom metric counts, indexed log volume, and host counts, each with a threshold set below your budgeted level.


When[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) receives the alert and posts to a chat channel or opens a ticket assigned to the owning team, a month-end surprise becomes a same-day fix.


The run is the meter there: Activepieces' pricing page lists one credit per flow run whether the flow has two steps or ten, while Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module.


That matters on a bill like this one, because a flow that checks the alert, looks up the owning team, formats the message and files the ticket as separate steps costs the same as one crammed into a single step.


The free plan covers 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, enough for a usage-alert flow.
